title: String charAt: Character at Position
description: Given a string str and a 0-based index pos, use str.charAt(pos) to return the character at that position. Return empty string if pos is out of bounds.
patternExplanation: .charAt(index) extracts character at an index, safely returning an empty string if index is out of bounds.

title: String charCodeAt: ASCII Code of Character
description: Given a string str and index idx, use str.charCodeAt(idx) to return the UTF-16 / ASCII code point integer.
patternExplanation: .charCodeAt(idx) retrieves the numeric ASCII/UTF-16 value of the character.

title: String at: Negative Index Access
description: Given a string str and positive integer k, use str.at(-k) to return the k-th character from the end. If str is shorter than k, return undefined.
patternExplanation: String.prototype.at() supports negative indices counting backwards from the end of the string.

title: String indexOf: Find Substring Position
description: Given string text and substring target, use text.indexOf(target) to return the 0-based starting index of the first occurrence of target. Return -1 if not found.
patternExplanation: .indexOf(target) returns the start position of the target substring, or -1 if absent.

title: String lastIndexOf: Last Substring Position
description: Given string text and substring target, use text.lastIndexOf(target) to return the index of the last occurrence of target.
patternExplanation: .lastIndexOf() searches backwards from the end of the string to find the final occurrence.

title: String startsWith: Verify HTTPS URL
description: Given a string url, use url.startsWith('https://') to check if it begins with the secure protocol prefix.
patternExplanation: .startsWith(prefix) checks for string prefix match without regular expressions.

title: String endsWith: Validate File Extension
description: Given string filename and extension ext, use filename.endsWith(ext) to check if the file ends with that extension.
patternExplanation: .endsWith(suffix) performs exact end-of-string matching cleanly.

title: String includes: Case-Insensitive Search
description: Given string text and keyword, check if keyword appears in text ignoring case by converting both with .toLowerCase().
patternExplanation: Normalizing both strings with toLowerCase() before calling .includes() normalizes text for search.

title: String startsWith: Position Offset
description: Given string str, substring prefix, and integer pos, use str.startsWith(prefix, pos) to check if prefix begins at position pos.
patternExplanation: Providing the position parameter checks prefix match at an internal index.

title: String endsWith: Up to Target Length
description: Given string str, suffix, and integer len, use str.endsWith(suffix, len) to verify if the string up to length len ends with suffix.
patternExplanation: The length parameter treats the string as if it were truncated to that length before checking endsWith.

title: String slice: Extract First Word
description: Given a sentence string sentence, use sentence.indexOf(' ') and sentence.slice() to extract the first word. If there is no space, return the entire string.
patternExplanation: Combining indexOf to find a boundary with .slice() extracts the first token cleanly.

title: String slice: Strip First and Last Characters
description: Given string text with at least 2 characters, return the string with its first and last character removed using text.slice(1, -1). If text has length <= 2, return "".
patternExplanation: .slice(1, -1) trims off the boundary characters on both sides.

title: String slice: Extract File Extension
description: Given filename string, find the last dot ('.') using lastIndexOf and return the extension including the dot (e.g. '.js'). If no dot exists, return ''.
patternExplanation: Using lastIndexOf to find the final dot ensures handling files with multiple dots correctly.

title: String substring: Extract Range with Auto-Swap
description: Given string str and indices start and end, use str.substring(start, end) to return the characters between them. Note that substring automatically swaps arguments if start > end.
patternExplanation: .substring() swaps start and end if start > end and treats negative arguments as 0.

title: String slice: Truncate with Ellipsis
description: Given text string and integer maxLen, if text.length > maxLen, return text.slice(0, maxLen) + '...'. Otherwise return text unchanged.
whatShouldHappen: If text.length > maxLen, return text.slice(0, maxLen) + '...'.
patternExplanation: Checking length against maximum display budget and appending an ellipsis is the standard snippet preview pattern.

title: String padStart: Zero-Pad Integer
description: Given a non-negative integer num and target length targetLen, return String(num) padded on the left with '0' using padStart.
patternExplanation: .padStart(targetLength, padChar) pads leading characters until target length is satisfied.

title: String padEnd: Right-Pad Column
description: Given text string and target width width, return text padded on the right with spaces (' ') using text.padEnd(width, ' ').
patternExplanation: .padEnd(width, padString) pads trailing characters, useful for tabular formatting in terminal displays.

title: String repeat: Build Divider Line
description: Given string pattern and integer count, use pattern.repeat(count) to generate a repeated divider string. If count <= 0, return "".
patternExplanation: .repeat(count) replicates a string sequence count times in constant JS engine allocation.

title: String padStart: Mask Sensitive Card
description: Given a credit card number string cardNum of length >= 4, keep only the last 4 characters and replace all preceding characters with '*' using padStart.
whatShouldHappen: Pad with '*' to full cardNum.length using .padStart(cardNum.length, '*').
patternExplanation: Extracting trailing digits and padding the difference with asterisks is the standard data sanitization pattern.

title: String repeat: Build Character Staircase
description: Given char string and total rows, return an array of strings where row i (from 1 to rows) contains char repeated i times.
patternExplanation: Using loop index i as the count in char.repeat(i) builds stepped sequence structures.

title: String trim: Clean Input Whitespace
description: Given string text, return text with all leading and trailing whitespace removed using text.trim().
patternExplanation: .trim() removes spaces, tabs, and newlines from both ends of a string.

title: String trimStart: Remove Leading Spaces
description: Given string text, remove only the leading whitespace while keeping any trailing whitespace intact using text.trimStart().
patternExplanation: .trimStart() leaves trailing formatting intact while sanitizing initial indentations.

title: String trimEnd: Remove Trailing Spaces
description: Given string text, remove only the trailing whitespace using text.trimEnd().
patternExplanation: .trimEnd() strips line-ending whitespace without disturbing initial indentation.

title: String Split & Join: Normalize Multi-Spaces
description: Given a string text containing consecutive spaces, return text where all contiguous sequences of whitespace are collapsed into single spaces, and trimmed.
whatShouldHappen: Filter with Boolean to remove empty segments.
patternExplanation: Splitting by spaces, filtering out empty strings, and rejoining with single spaces normalizes whitespace effortlessly.

title: String replaceAll: Remove Newlines
description: Given a multiline string text, use text.replaceAll('\n', ' ') to replace all newline characters with a single space.
patternExplanation: .replaceAll() eliminates all instances of a target character string without requiring regex flags.

title: String slice: Capitalize First Letter
description: Given word string, capitalize its first letter and keep the remaining letters lowercase. Return empty string if word is empty.
patternExplanation: Combining char[0].toUpperCase() with slice(1).toLowerCase() establishes standard capitalized casing.

title: String map: Title Case Every Word
description: Given a space-separated sentence string, return the sentence with the first letter of each word capitalized and the rest lowercase.
whatShouldHappen: Split sentence into words with sentence.split(' ').
Map each word: w ? w[0].toUpperCase() + w.slice(1).toLowerCase() : "".
patternExplanation: Splitting words, capitalizing each, and joining with spaces creates standard headline typography.

title: String Loop: Toggle Case of Characters
description: Given string str, return a new string where all uppercase characters become lowercase, and lowercase characters become uppercase.
patternExplanation: Comparing each character against its upper-case form reveals casing and directs the inversion.

title: String: Check if Entirely Uppercase
description: Given string str containing at least one alphabetical character, return true if str === str.toUpperCase() and false otherwise.
whatShouldHappen: Check if str === str.toUpperCase() and has at least one letter.
patternExplanation: Equality with str.toUpperCase() and inequality with str.toLowerCase() verifies all-caps alphabetical content.

title: String replace: camelCase to kebab-case
description: Given camelCase string str (e.g. 'fontSize'), convert it to kebab-case (e.g. 'font-size') using replace with regex.
patternExplanation: Regex replacement functions insert delimiters before matched uppercase letters, transforming naming conventions.

title: String split: Parse Comma-Separated Values
description: Given a CSV record string line, use line.split(',') to parse it into an array of string values.
patternExplanation: .split(",") tokenizes character-separated data into indexed array elements.

title: String split & reverse: Invert Word Order
description: Given a space-separated sentence string, return a new string with the order of words reversed.
patternExplanation: The split-reverse-join pipeline is the classic idiom for inverting word sequences.

title: String filter: Count Target Word Frequency
description: Given text and targetWord, split text by spaces and count how many words match targetWord (case-insensitive).

traceTable.inputLabel: text = 'the cat and the dog', targetWord = 'the'

patternExplanation: Tokenizing by word boundaries and counting matching elements provides text frequency analysis.

title: String spread: Convert String to Characters Array
description: Given string str, use array spread [...str] to return an array of its individual characters.
patternExplanation: Spreading a string into an array correctly handles full Unicode code points unlike legacy charAt loops.

title: Array join: Assemble Filepath
description: Given an array of path segment strings segments, use segments.join('/') to combine them into a slash-separated path.
patternExplanation: .join("/") joins directory and path tokens with consistent delimiters.

title: String replace: Swap First Match
description: Given string text, target substring target, and replacement repl, use text.replace(target, repl) to replace the first occurrence of target.
patternExplanation: .replace(string, replacement) replaces only the first occurrence of a string pattern.

title: String replaceAll: Substitute Every Occurrence
description: Given string text, target substring target, and replacement repl, use text.replaceAll(target, repl) to replace all occurrences of target.
patternExplanation: .replaceAll() updates all occurrences of a string without requiring global regexes.

title: String replace: Strip English Vowels
description: Given a string text, use text.replace(/[aeiou]/gi, '') to remove all English vowels (case-insensitive).
patternExplanation: Using regular expression character classes [aeiou] with global and ignore-case flags removes character subsets.

title: String replaceAll: Censor Target Word
description: Given string sentence and badWord, replace every occurrence of badWord with an asterisk string of matching length ('*'.repeat(badWord.length)).
patternExplanation: Generating dynamic length masks with repeat and applying replaceAll redacts sensitive words securely.

title: String Chained replaceAll: Escape Basic HTML
description: Given string str, escape '&' to '&', '<' to '<', and '>' to '>' using chained replaceAll calls in order.
patternExplanation: Escaping ampersands first followed by angle brackets avoids double-encoding entities in HTML sanitization.
